text:
tariq: Heads up — saw KV-cache thrash on the paged FlashAttention variant when batch_size > 48 on A100s. L3 tiler appears to be spilling and causing memory-bandwidth backpressure.

emily: Can you paste the profiler dump or the minimal repro command? which kernel shows the stall?

tariq: Quick paste from a run (nvprof-like):
```
model=flashx-paged-v2, batch=64, seq=512
kernel=flash_paginated_fused_v2
SMEM usage: 92KB/96KB
L2 BW: 1.28TB/s (saturated)
L3 tiler spills: 38% of tiles -> increased evictions
KV hit: 98% -> 72% (after 30s)
stall_reason: mem_pipe_wait / outstanding loads
```

juan: sounds like tiler is allocating tiles that push the working set out of the KV window. try lowering tile_w/tile_h or disable L3 tiler to confirm. also check batch coalescing upstream — big merged batches can widen seq-length distribution. :mag:

perf-bot: [regression-alert] flashx-paged-v2 p95 latency +12% since job 1999995000, correlated with recent tiler heuristics change.

sophia: Do we know if the prefetcher churn increased? eviction storms from prefetchers can amplify bandwidth.

tariq: Yes — prefetch churn up ~3.2x in the same trace window. KV eviction rate jumps after each large batch allocation. Prefetcher queued requests also spike.

emily: Quick test plan:
- run microbench with --tiler=off vs --tiler=on (same batch seq distribution)
- try tile_w=64 and tile_w=32 knobs
- enable --kv-prefetch=on/off to measure churn
- collect nvprof + nvtx ranges and token-level KV hit timeline
Command: `./bench/attention_bench --model flashx-paged-v2 --batch 64 --seq 512 --tiler off --nvtx`

juan: Also add a run that forces small batches but same aggregate throughput to see if it's purely batch-size or coalescing.

tariq: Running now on 4xA100. I'll drop results here in ~20m and open a perf ticket. created placeholder perf issue: RED-4567.

[20m later]

tariq: Quick results: disabling tiler removed the eviction storm and restored KV hit to ~96%. p95 back to baseline. Downsides: overall token throughput down ~6% (tiler gives more aggressive packing normally).

sophia: That's actionable. Proposed mitigation: add an adaptive tiler safety net — monitor short-window KV-hit and L2 BW; if KV-hit < 80% or L2 BW > threshold for 10s, fall back to conservative tiling or disable tiler for that model/instance. Also add a canary: run fallback locally on a small % of requests first.

emily: Can we implement as a routing policy? i.e., mark instances with tiler=aggressive and add runtime fallback in the dispatcher. Simpler than sweeping configs.

juan: We should also explore tiler micro-optimizations: reduce SMEM per tile, avoid spilling path for common seq lengths, and tweak pipeline stages to decouple prefetch from tiler allocation decisions.

tariq: Action items: RED-4567 track microbench artifacts + nvprof tar, RED-4570 for runtime fallback feature, add test in perf suite to catch KV-hit regressions. I'll upload logs to the ticket.

sophia: Nice. tagging @eng-runtime-owners and adding a short README in the perf artifacts so oncall can triage quicker if we see the regression again. :white_check_mark:

emily: Thanks — keep us posted.

[thread closed for now]
